input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 conditions our ability to engage any other provider on first disclosing and matching for Vendor any more favourable offer we receive. That is a de facto exclusivity / right-of-first-refusal binding the Customer: we cannot freely buy from another supplier without first routing the competing terms through Cobalt. It is unlimited in scope, applies for the full term, and has no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (defined product category, 12 months, automatic end on service-level or delivery failure). It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, which states that Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment, so deletion of 7.2 restores internal consistency as well as the preferred position. The most-favoured-pricing aspect of the same sentence is addressed under the MFN rule and is not double-counted here; no other clause imposes exclusivity on us (Sections 13.1 and 14.2 concern licence scope and ownership, not supplier freedom).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted Section 7.2 because requiring us to disclose and match any better offer before engaging another provider operates as a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal, which our playbook does not accept and which contradicts Section 12.3's confirmation that we have given no exclusivity commitment. If Cobalt needs something here, we can discuss a narrow arrangement limited to a defined service category, capped at twelve months, and terminating automatically if service levels or delivery dates are missed.
proposal.summary: Delete Section 7.2's disclose-and-match condition on engaging another provider (de facto exclusivity/ROFR).
